name: initiative_under_goal
description: Two leaves share the SAME top-level goal; only an initiative in between differs in importance. Distinguishes a formula that reads the whole ancestor chain from one that reads only the top-level ancestor (which sees the identical root for both and cannot produce the stated order) -- see notes for why the leaves' own importance has to stay close at the current 0.93/0.07 weighting for that to still hold.

nodes.label: Strategic goal both leaves sit under
Initiative under the shared goal, deprioritized after a reorg
Initiative under the same shared goal, still important

notes: Both leaves sit under the identical top-level goal (goal_shared, 0.9); only the intermediate initiative differs (0.95 vs 0.1). At the original 0.5*own + 0.5*mean(ancestors) weighting, the leaves' own importance could differ by a wide margin (0.5 vs 0.6) and the initiative gap still decided the order. Revised down to 0.93*own + 0.07*mean(ancestors) (review on #474) made the own-importance weight dominant enough that a 0.1 gap there (0.93*0.1=0.093) outweighed the 0.85 initiative-importance gap once discounted to 7% (0.07*0.85=0.0595) -- own importance alone decided the order, defeating the fixture's point. Fixed by narrowing the own-importance gap to 0.02 instead (0.5 vs 0.52, scaled by 0.93 = 0.0186) so the intermediate initiative's effect (scaled by 0.07) can still win: task_under_important_initiative = 0.93*0.5 + 0.07*mean(0.95, 0.9) = 0.465 + 0.06475 = 0.52975; task_under_deprioritized_initiative = 0.93*0.52 + 0.07*mean(0.1, 0.9) = 0.4836 + 0.035 = 0.5186. important now outranks deprioritized, and a root-only formula (which would see the identical 0.9 root for both and fall back to own importance: deprioritized 0.5466 > important 0.528) gets this backwards -- restoring the fixture's original diagnostic power, not just a passing arithmetic check.
